summary.headline: Campus Activewear Q1 FY27: revenue up 12.2%, volume up 11.7%, EBITDA margin 15.9%, PAT up 17.7%, with ASP drag from temporary accounting and mix effects.
summary.overview: Campus reported 12.2% revenue growth, 11.7% volume growth, 15.9% EBITDA margin and 17.7% PAT growth in Q1 FY27. Reported ASP growth was held back by a Walmart (Flipkart/Myntra) GT-charge netting change (about 2.5%) and a school-shoe mix shift (about 2%), both described as Q1-only effects. An 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 gave underlying core-category ASP growth of about 5%. Management guided to mid-double-digit FY27 growth, split between ASP and volume, and reiterated a 17-19% EBITDA margin aspiration. Record Q1 production and record distributor orders were highlighted ahead of the festive season.

financial_highlights.change: Management says about 4.5-5% was temporary (GT netting ~2%, franchise SOR transition ~2.5%); normalised growth about 4%-plus ex these factors per management's framing
Analyst-cited figure; management did not dispute it

financial_highlights.metric: ASP impact from Walmart GT netting
Underlying ASP increase, core Stuck-On category
Additional depreciation from Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants
Minimum wage cost in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: about Rs. 5 crore for the quarter

financial_highlights.change: About 10% annualisation and increments, about 5% new hiring

segments.name: Stuck-On (core)
segments.commentary: Underlying ASP up about 5% after ~8% MRP increase; school shoes moved from DIP into Stuck-On, which management says has higher ASP and margin than DIP.

segments.name: School shoes
segments.commentary: Revenue up nearly 50% YoY; about 40% of Q1 volume growth came from this category, expected to normalise from Q2.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Q1 contributed about 12-13% of volume; management targets about 30% growth for the category in FY27, down from near-100% historically.

segments.name: Open footwear (sandals/slippers)
segments.commentary: Slower growth, about 4-5% below rest of category, attributed to CNG/LPG supply constraints affecting hot-and-cold machines during the war-related period.

segments.name: Franchise (FOFO/SOR)
segments.commentary: Management cited about 25% de-growth in franchise revenue in Q1 from the outright-to-SOR model transition across 158 stores (about 2.5% revenue impact); 18 EBOs opened in Q1, the highest in 6-8 quarters.

segments.name: Marketplace and brand.com
segments.commentary: Marketplace operations up mid-double digits; brand.com up over 100% YoY; company-owned stores SSG about 20%.

segments.name: General trade Gujarat
segments.commentary: GT grew at least 20-25% faster than rest of country over the period; Maharashtra now second-largest GT state after UP.

segments.name: Elan by Campus
segments.commentary: Neo-casual launch about 60 days old, priced Rs. 1,899-2,599, selling in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com; next set planned for festive season.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: mid-double-digit overall revenue growth, split between ASP and volume; management said volume is expected to be high single digit and ASP growth of at least 6-7% from Q2 onwards.
Management is '100% confident' of delivering the 17-19% EBITDA margin band for FY27.
Store additions target: about 90-100 stores by end FY27 (guidance range 80-120).
Employee cost as % of sales expected to be proportionate to FY26; no further incremental wage cost expected beyond what is already baked in.
Festive timing: Diwali in November 2026; BBD shifts to October from September, so some marketplace revenue may move from Q2 to Q3.
Management does not plan further MRP increases; expects raw material cost relief to flow into P&L as volatility subsides.
capex_capacity: Record Q1 production, with July 2026 the highest-ever production month, to build festive inventory.
Installed annual capacity cited at about 31 million pairs, down from 36 million two years ago, due to shutdown of about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity.
New manufacturing facilities at Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar commissioned and ramping up; sneakers production also from Haridwar and Pantnagar.
Franchise EBO ROI cited at 18-30% depending on store economics; franchisees pay deposit on inventory, company controls inventory, discounting and replenishment.
Franchise master partners to rise from about 8-9 to about 16; about 8 new partners added this year.
demand_pricing: 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 across key categories; management says volumes grew despite it and resistance has been limited. No further hikes planned.
Management said some demand tapering was seen in the last quarter, citing geopolitical factors and floods in Maharashtra and Gujarat, but its demand reading remains positive.
Record orders at the distributor meet held in May 2026, giving visibility on festive demand.
Management sees some constraints at smaller organised and unorganised competitors due to working-capital stress, though impact on festive supply is unclear.

Price-point mix: management said Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core shoe segment; analyst pointed to about 7% two-year CAGR decline in sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue, which management attributed to the 8% price hike shifting products above Rs. 1,500 and reporting changes.

qa_highlights.question: Vidisha Seth (Ambit): Is the 8% MRP hike, above industry levels, risking volume or share given elasticity in economy key products, and will there be another hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8% is a fair hike, accepted with limited resistance, and volumes grew despite it; RM inflation has been fully absorbed and no further MRP hikes will be taken. Raw-material relief is expected to flow back into P&L as markets stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash (Motilal Oswal): Why did sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue decline about 7% on a two-year CAGR basis, and is the company exiting price points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not exiting price points and Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core; the decline reflects products moving above Rs. 1,500 after the 8% hike, a change in reporting, and faster closed-shoe growth versus open footwear. Gaps at economy price points are being filled over the next couple of months before the season.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash: Why did installed capacity fall from 36 million to 31 million pairs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity were shut as uneconomic; school shoes were moved from DIP into Stuck-On, which has higher ASP and margin. Stuck-On capacity is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta (Kotak): How much did school shoes contribute to volume growth, and is the margin 17-19% band still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: School shoes contributed about 40% of Q1 volume growth and will normalise from Q2. Management targets FY27 mid-double-digit growth split between ASP (at least 6-7% from Q2) and volume, and said it is 100% confident of the 17-19% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta: What drove the faster growth in other expenses excluding A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gupta said about Rs. 5 crore was minimum-wage cost, about Rs. 2.5 crore was advertising and marketing (distributor meet and logo launch), and about Rs. 2.5 crore was depreciation/indirect cost from the new Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (Emkay): Why is EBITDA growth 11% when revenue growth is about 15-16% ex-accounting changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Walmart GT netting is an accounting change with no absolute EBITDA impact. Employee cost rose about 15% (10% annualisation and increments, 5% new hiring) plus higher SG&A, which drove the gap. FY27 employee cost as % of sales is expected to be in line with FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Shraddha Kapadia (SMFS): Can volume growth stay double-digit for FY27, and what is the Elan by Campus traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not promise double-digit volume but said volume will be high single digit, with ASP and volume together delivering mid-double-digit revenue growth. Elan, about 60 days old at Rs. 1,899-2,599, sells in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com, with a second set planned for festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Prerna Jhunjhunwala (Elara): What is the store opening plan, and how do franchise economics work under the SOR model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 90-100 openings in FY27 (range 80-120), with master franchise partners rising from about 8-9 to about 16. Under SOR, the company controls inventory and discounting, franchisees pay an inventory deposit and bear rent, and EBO ROI is about 18-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Ajay Nandavar (individual investor): Why is open footwear growing slower, and how does Gujarat franchise growth coexist with trade growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandals use hot-and-cold machines dependent on CNG/LPG, which were constrained during the war period, so growth is about 4-5% below the rest of the category. Management said franchise stores have not cannibalised GT, which grew at least 20-25% faster than the rest of the country in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (follow-up): Is the 8% hike in line with industry, and what signs show consumer acceptance and lower competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers took similar or slightly lower hikes; the May distributor meet recorded record orders after the hike. Management cited marketplace growth in the mid-double digits, company-owned store SSG of about 20% and brand.com growth above 100%, and said some smaller and unorganised players faced production constraints due to working-capital stress.

risks_watch: Sustainability of ASP recovery to 6-7% from Q2: the 2.5% Walmart GT netting and 2% school-shoe mix effects must reverse as stated, and the 8% hike must hold without volume loss.
Volume normalisation after school shoes (about 40% of Q1 volume growth) taper, against a high-single-digit FY27 volume target.
EBITDA growth (11%) lagging revenue growth; the 17-19% margin band depends on employee cost (about 15% growth) and SG&A staying in line with FY26 and on raw-material relief.
Demand tapering noted in the last quarter (geopolitics, Maharashtra and Gujarat floods); record festive inventory built in Q1 and July raises inventory-risk exposure if festive demand disappoints.
Franchise transition: about 25% franchise de-growth in Q1 across 158 stores; the SOR model's accounting and store-opening pace (90-100 target) need to be tracked.
Sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue two-year CAGR decline of about 7%; management says economy price-point gaps will be filled before the season.
Elan by Campus and sneaker growth (about 30% target) are early-stage; the Diwali and Big Billion Day shift (October) may move some marketplace revenue from Q2 to Q3.
key_quotes: So, we are, yes, we will be close to double-digit. We cannot promise a double-digit volume growth, but it will be high single digits for sure, right?
Absolutely, Umang. Yes, we are 100% confident of delivering that. There is no reason not to deliver the margin.
RM inflation has been fully absorbed.
So, it is just a recalibration of the DIP.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY27 targets, margin band and festive visibility, with 100% confidence stated on the 17-19% EBITDA margin. Cautious and somewhat evasive on the precise drivers of the 11% EBITDA growth gap, on the sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue decline and on demand tapering; several answers were deferred to offline follow-up.

Store additions: about 90-100 stores by end FY27 (range 80-120); 18 EBOs opened in Q1

growth.why: FY27 guided to mid-double-digit revenue growth (midpoint ~12% assumed) split into high-single-digit volume and at least 6-7% ASP from Q2, backed by an 8% MRP hike, record distributor orders, record Q1 production and 90-100 store additions, though capacity is not quantified and management flagged demand tapering across categories.
